key_insight: LUCQUE introduces a large, comprehensively annotated lung cancer screening dataset from Québec. It aims to make AI evaluation more reproducible, comparable, and independently verifiable.
problem_solved: Lung cancer screening AI has often been evaluated using private or fragmented public datasets with inconsistent clinical information and expert nodule annotations, making reliable comparisons difficult.
method: Build a dataset from low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lung cancer screening in Québec.
Provide comprehensive annotations to address gaps in existing evaluation datasets.
Support reproducible comparisons and independent assessment of screening AI tools.
impact: LUCQUE could give AI/ML practitioners a stronger foundation for benchmarking lung cancer screening tools. The supplied abstract is truncated, so dataset size, access conditions, and validation results cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Québec map linked to a lung CT image to illustrate the dataset's origin.
Pipeline diagram: LDCT screening → annotated dataset → AI evaluation.
Side-by-side comparison of fragmented datasets versus a comprehensively annotated dataset.
Three icons representing reproducibility, comparability, and independent assessment.
paper_title: LUCQUE: A lung cancer screening dataset from Québec for reliable AI evaluation
paper_authors: Johanna Topalis, Yannick Lemaréchal, Gabriel Couture, Hanife Ersay, Loran Nas
